units.passage: Students are expected to provide attribution for any text created using generative AI tools as appropriate.
units.policy: Students are expected to provide attribution for any text created using generative AI tools as appropriate.
units.why: "Students are expected to provide attribution for any text created using generative AI tools" requires acknowledgement of AI use, P24.

units.passage: Any student work submitted using AI tools should clearly indicate what work is the student’s work and what part is generated by the AI.
units.policy: In the quoted Colorado sample, student work submitted using AI tools should clearly indicate which part is the student's and which part is AI-generated.
units.why: Quoted Colorado template: "Any student work submitted using AI tools should clearly indicate what work is the student's work and what part is generated by the AI" marks AI parts in the submission, P24.

units.passage: When you submit your assignment, I expect you to clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool (e.g., AI-generated text appears in a different colored font, quoted directly in the text, or use an in-text parenthetical citation).
units.policy: In the quoted UMass Amherst sample, students clearly attribute which text was generated by the AI tool, for example in a different colored font, direct quotation, or an in-text parenthetical citation.
units.why: The passage asks students to attribute AI-generated text, with colored font, direct quotation or an in-text parenthetical citation as examples ('I expect you to clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool'). That is disclosure attached to a submission, so it is a student-addressed, during-work requirement of type P24; P27 is about marking AI-derived code and this passage concerns text

units.passage: To be consistent with our scholarly values, students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work and use quotation marks or other appropriate indicators of quoted material when appropriate.
units.policy: In the quoted Iowa sample, students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work and use quotation marks or other appropriate indicators of quoted material when appropriate.
units.why: Quoted Iowa full-use template: "students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work" requires citation, P24.

units.passage: Inform instructors of AI tool use and explain how they were used.
units.policy: Students inform instructors of AI tool use and explain how they were used.
units.why: "Inform instructors of AI tool use and explain how they were used" requires disclosure to the instructor, P24.

units.passage: Just like any other source, AI-generated content should be cited.
units.policy: Just like any other source, AI-generated content should be cited.
units.why: "Just like any other source, AI-generated content should be cited" asks for citation; P24 chosen over P45 because the rule is about citation, not collaboration.

units.passage: If you are going to allow your students to use generative AI as a source in their academic work, you may want to consider requiring your students to clearly disclose the role generative AI played in formulating their work.
units.why: 'you may want to consider requiring your students to clearly disclose the role generative AI played in formulating their work': a disclosure with each submission, P24, as a suggestion.

units.passage: (ii) unacknowledged use of materials prepared by another person or by an individual or company engaged in the selling of term papers or other academic materials; or
units.why: Plagiarism defined as 'unacknowledged use of materials prepared by another person' or a company; AI is not named, so this is the general acknowledgment duty. Closest is P24 (acknowledge use), though only partly.
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI; general duty to credit others' work, which the AI section builds on.

units.passage: use by paraphrase or direct quotation of the published work of another source without properly crediting the author or source with footnotes, citations or bibliographical reference
units.why: The plagiarism definition says use of another source 'without properly crediting' is plagiarism; for AI this implies citation, but AI is not named, so disclosure type P24 fits only partly.
units.fit_note: General plagiarism citation rule; AI is not named, so it applies to AI only by implication.

units.passage: If the work was a product of collaboration, each student is expected to clearly acknowledge in writing all persons who contributed to its completion
units.why: The rule that students must 'clearly acknowledge in writing all persons who contributed' sets disclosure for collaboration; P24 is the nearest type though AI is not named.
units.fit_note: Acknowledgement of human collaborators; AI is not named.

units.passage: An expectation for our students is that there is accurate and transparent attribution of AI use in their classroom assessments.
units.why: "An expectation for our students is that there is accurate and transparent attribution of AI use in their classroom assessments" tells students to attribute AI use in their graded work. It is an expectation ("expected" is should), so modality should; P24 (disclose with each submission); the work is assignments, not exams, so during-work; disclosure expected of students is unit_stance require.

units.passage: Students are allowed to use advanced automated tools (artificial intelligence or machine learning tools such as ChatGPT, Co-Pilot, or Dall-E) on assignments in this course if instructor permission is obtained in advance. Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools. C. AI Use only with acknowledgement Students are allowed to use advanced automated tools (artificial intelligence or machine learning tools such as ChatGPT, Co-Pilot, or Dall-E) on assignments in this course if that use is properly documented and credited.
units.why: Option C allows tools "if that use is properly documented and credited"; the condition is acknowledgement, so P24.

units.passage: Ethical dimension: Students using AI should be transparent about their use and make sure it aligns with academic integrity.
units.why: The Gladd example's ethical principle, "Students using AI should be transparent about their use", is a disclosure expectation quoted as a model rationale, so P24.
units.fit_note: Quoted as an example instructor rationale, not as a WSU rule.

units.passage: Another could be adding a question to an application as to whether AI was used in any way and to explain how.
units.why: The report suggests "adding a question to an application as to whether AI was used in any way and to explain how", an applicant disclosure rule; P24 fits though for applications, not coursework.
units.fit_note: Applies to admission and hiring applicants, not to coursework submissions. Disclosure in job or graduate applications, not coursework.

units.passage: Human Resources & Admissions • Observation #4 – Human Resources o We need to keep tabs on HR trends with AI misuse. o Adding a question about AI usage on applications could be useful for understanding how applicants use AI. ▪ We may need to provide guidelines for how AI should or should not be used in the application packet. o More discussion is needed with using AI for data analysis. • Observation #5 – Undergraduate Admissions o We need to provide guidelines for how AI should or should not be used in the application essay. o We could require a question at the end of the application that asks an applicant whether they have used AI in any way as part of the application and/or essay, and if so, to explain how and why. • Observation #6 – Graduate Admissions o We need to provide guidelines for how AI should or should not be used in the application process, including the writing sample. o We could propose a change to the BOG statute that includes concerns about authenticity. Computing & Information Technology (C&IT) • Observation #7 – C&IT o We need to provide the WSU community with guidelines for navigating AI tools. o The Senate’s Facilities, Support Services & Technology Committee needs to take up the discussion of developing, integrating, maintaining, and using these AI tools and systems specific to WSU. Privacy Officer • Observation #8 – Privacy o We need to develop a website dedicated to privacy tips, cautions, and information for the WSU community. o We need to educate our
units.why: The report suggests "a required question at the end of the application that asks an applicant whether they have used AI", a disclosure rule for applicants (P24).
units.fit_note: Applies to applicants. Applicants disclose AI use in admissions essays.

units.passage: You need to explicitly state at the beginning of the assignment when, why, and how you have used AI.
units.why: The graduate template repeats the disclosure of when, why and how AI was used, a disclosure with each submission (P24).

units.passage: You need to explicitly state at the beginning of the assignment when, why, and how you have used AI.
units.why: The template says students "need to explicitly state at the beginning of the assignment when, why, and how you have used AI", a disclosure duty (P24).

units.passage: Documenting AI’s use in an assignment is your responsibility.
units.why: The graduate template says students must document AI use ("documenting AI's use in an assignment is your responsibility"), a disclosure duty (P24).

units.passage: Asking applicants to disclose whether they used AI in any aspect of the application process should be included in the application, regardless of their position, and provided to the hiring committee for consideration.
units.why: Asking applicants whether they used AI 'should be included in the application, regardless of their position' is applicant disclosure (P24).
units.fit_note: Disclosure by job applicants.

units.passage: and disclosed thro ugh appropriate referencing or citation.
units.why: The exception also requires that use be "disclosed through appropriate referencing or citation", a disclosure rule (P24).
units.fit_note: Condition within the cheating definition.

units.passage: When AI use is permitted, its use in coursework must be properly acknowledged by the student, and failure to do so is also a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: 'its use in coursework must be properly acknowledged by the student' requires disclosure of permitted AI use; student, during-work, must. P24 (disclosure with each submission) fits; P25 would require tool/prompt detail that is not stated.

units.passage: When AI use is permitted, its use in coursework must be properly acknowledged by the student, and failure to do so is also a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: 'its use in coursework must be properly acknowledged by the student' requires disclosure of permitted AI use; student, during-work, must. P24 (disclosure with each submission) fits; P25 would require tool/prompt detail that is not stated.

units.passage: Maximally encouraging AI policies should instruct students to appropriately acknowledge and cite their use of these tools.
units.why: 'Maximally encouraging AI policies should instruct students to appropriately acknowledge and cite their use' tells instructors that an encouraging policy must carry a disclosure duty for students. It is advice to instructors writing policy (before-course, should) about acknowledgement and citation (P24), and the position it recommends is that students acknowledge use (require).

units.passage: Be transparent about AI usage when it has contributed to your work product to help maintain academic standards and support the use of AI to enhance, not replace original thinking.
units.why: "Be transparent about AI usage when it has contributed to your work product" recommends disclosure of AI contribution, P24.
units.fit_note: Also says AI should enhance, not replace, original thinking (P32).

units.passage: When deciding about whether to be transparent or not regarding AI use ask yourself this question, “would a reasonable person expect to know that AI was used to create this item?”
units.why: 'would a reasonable person expect to know that AI was used to create this item?' gives a test for when to be transparent; recommends disclosure (P24), with the test noted as a partial fit.
units.fit_note: Gives a reasonable-person test for deciding whether to disclose rather than a flat requirement. Gives a reasonable-person test for when to disclose rather than a rule to disclose all use.

units.passage: Being transparent about your use of AI is important because it develops and maintains trust and credibility for all stakeholders
units.why: Transparency "develops and maintains trust and credibility for all stakeholders" gives a reason for disclosure; P24 is nearest since there is no fairness (P95) or skill claim.
units.fit_note: Rationale is trust, credibility and the scholarly practice of showing your work, not fairness to other students. Gives reasons for disclosing: trust, the academic tradition of citing, protection of copyrighted work, awareness of AI mistakes.

units.passage: Students communicate the ways they engage with and use AI tools in support of their learning process and any products they create.
units.why: Students 'communicate the ways they engage with and use AI tools in support of their learning process and any products they create' describes student transparency; disclosure, P24.

units.passage: It is your decision (except where it is a requirement for a course or job) to disclose use of AI.
units.why: 'It is your decision (except where it is a requirement for a course or job) to disclose use of AI' makes disclosure optional unless required; a rule on whether disclosure is mandatory, P24.
units.fit_note: Makes disclosure the user's choice unless a course or job requires it, the opposite of a blanket requirement. Says disclosure is the user's choice unless a course or job requires it; the type assumes a required disclosure.

units.passage: If required, cite your use of AI. Examples of Formal Citation Standards for AI .
units.why: "If required, cite your use of AI" is a conditional citation duty, P24.
units.fit_note: The duty applies only where a course or other setting requires citation.

units.passage: Acknowledge when and how you used them
units.why: "Acknowledge when and how you used them" requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.fit_note: Used in First Year Experience courses (an in-use example).

units.passage: When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment.
units.why: 'When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment' tells students to disclose when unsure; P24.
units.fit_note: A when-unsure rule that leans to disclosure rather than asking the instructor (P10). The advice for doubt is to disclose, not to ask the instructor.

units.passage: Properly cite AI-generated content in academic work.
units.why: 'Properly cite AI-generated content in academic work'; P24.

units.passage: However, the use of such tools must be documented and clearly cited in all submitted work
units.why: "the use of such tools must be documented and clearly cited in all submitted work" requires disclosure with each submission (P24).

units.passage: Students must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI and show how AI tools were used in the process of creating a final product
units.why: Students 'must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI and show how AI tools were used in the process of creating a final product' requires disclosure of AI-generated content with the submission, plus a description of process (P24).
units.fit_note: Also asks students to show how AI tools were used in the process, not only to identify output; it names no tool, prompt or date.

units.passage: When allowed, students must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI and show how AI tools were used in the process of creating a final product.
units.why: "When allowed, students must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI" requires disclosure when use is allowed (P24).

units.passage: When students are allowed to use generative AI tools, they may be required to cite the tools that are used and/or provide specific information about their use.
units.why: "they may be required to cite the tools that are used and/or provide specific information about their use" says instructors may require citation and details (P24).
units.fit_note: Phrased as something students may be required to do, depending on the instructor.

units.passage: Rather than all out prohibiting AI usage, one approach educators are using to address issues of information origin is to require students who use AI to reflect on and cite their use of AI tools
units.why: The page says 'one approach educators are using' is 'to require students who use AI to reflect on and cite their use of AI tools'. This offers requiring disclosure as an option to instructors who do not prohibit AI, so it is P24 with modality may.
units.fit_note: Also includes reflection and sharing process and prompts (P26, P25); presented as one approach educators use, not as a rule. Also mentions reflection and citing prompts (P25, P26).

units.passage: In accordance with university policies around academic integrity in the Student Code of Conduct, we will be transparent in our use of AI in the completion of any classroom tasks. And, although there are questions around how and whether to cite AI, we will reference our use in the following way.
units.why: Example 1: 'we will be transparent in our use of AI in the completion of any classroom tasks' requires disclosure for all tasks; P24.

units.passage: It is your responsibility, however, to be transparent in that use.
units.why: 'It is your responsibility, however, to be transparent in that use' places disclosure on the student, P24.

units.passage: You are also required, for every assignment in this course, to submit an “AI Acknowledgement”. AI Acknowledgement: For every assignment submission, you will include a 150-300 word acknowledgment. Your acknowledgement should include, 1. The identification of the tool(s) you used, 2. An explanation of why you decided to use the tool(s), 3. A description of how you used the tool(s) to manage assignment requirements, and 4. A reflection on your experience using the tool, exploring what worked or didn’t, and acknowledging limitations of the tool for this assignment, potential biases, etc.
units.why: The sample says 'you are required, for every assignment in this course, to submit an "AI Acknowledgement"'. A disclosure submitted with every assignment is P24; the content of the acknowledgement is coded as its own unit (P26).

units.passage: When you do use generative-AI tools, you must be fully transparent with your use, including proper citation and any other documentation required by your instructor.
units.why: Example 4: 'you must be fully transparent with your use, including proper citation and any other documentation required by your instructor' requires disclosure and citation, P24.

units.passage: and to use any approved tools transparently and with proper acknowledgment, consistent with academic integrity standards.
units.why: Students are to 'use any approved tools transparently and with proper acknowledgment', a disclosure duty, P24.

units.passage: AI-generated content used in an official State capacity should include transparency of authorship. This includes citation for content that is AI generated or edited, and should disclose details of its review (how the material was reviewed, edited, by whom, and the date the system was used).
units.why: AI content used in a state capacity should show authorship transparency and citation, with details of review: disclosure (P24).
units.fit_note: Also asks for review details (how, by whom, date) and covers state-capacity use.

units.passage: Clearly note when AI is used especially in publicly facing works representing the university.
units.why: "Clearly note when AI is used especially in publicly facing works representing the university" is a disclosure rule, P24.

units.passage: Develop a Practice of Transparency Faculty and students should cite their use of AI. When instructors thoughtfully acknowledge how AI has supported their work—in course design, writing, or research— they help students develop a more mature understanding of academic tools, agency, and intellectual ownership.
units.why: "Faculty and students should cite their use of AI" is a disclosure expectation for everyone: P24.

units.passage: At any level above UG 0, you must submit a written statement identifying any AI tools or AI-enabled features used and explaining how they were used in producing the work.
units.why: "you must submit a written statement identifying any AI tools or AI-enabled features used and explaining how they were used" requires disclosure with each submission (P24).

units.passage: Any AI use above UG 0 must be disclosed in writing.
units.why: "Any AI use above UG 0 must be disclosed in writing" is a disclosure requirement for submissions, P24.

units.passage: Because preparatory work is part of the assignment, this use must be disclosed.
units.why: "Because preparatory work is part of the assignment, this use must be disclosed" requires disclosure even of brainstorming (P24).

units.passage: A structured statement of work is ideal, but any written disclosure satisfies this requirement; what matters is that you put your AI use on the record and stand behind what you report.
units.why: "A structured statement of work is ideal, but any written disclosure satisfies this requirement" says what form disclosure may take, P24.

units.passage: Disclose the use of Generative AI tools: YU faculty and staff who leverage Generative AI to produce any written materials or other work product must disclose that those materials and that work product is based on or derives from the use of Generative AI. You must always be transparent if you are relying on the output of a Generative AI tool.
units.why: "YU faculty and staff who leverage Generative AI to produce any written materials or other work product must disclose" requires staff to disclose AI use (P24).
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty and staff work product, not student submissions.

units.passage: It contains information on how to write, citation practices and formats, and subject-specific writing. Citing Generative Artificial Intelligence in MLA or APA Style Are you in a class that allows the use of generative AI? You will need to cite your generative AI sources appropriately.
units.why: "You will need to cite your generative AI sources appropriately" with MLA/APA links requires citing AI use (P24).

units.passage: Any content produced using Generative AI must be cited appropriately (see: MLA and APA for examples).
units.why: "Any content produced using Generative AI must be cited appropriately" requires citation (P24).
